title: the Linux bus spawn runs the caller's own interpreter
intention: remote.py's systemd-run and setsid spawns start the bus with background_python(), the caller's own interpreter, as the Windows spawn already does.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 (Linux census): under PATH=/usr/bin:/bin the bare 'python3' at remote.py:214 found the system python, the bus died at bus.py:73 -> store.py:55 import psycopg2 (bus.log), and 29 proofs read 'no bus'.
traces_to: Law 3 (measured, 29 reds) and CP6 (the spawn's safety is built, not borrowed from PATH).
how: remote.py:214 (_spawn) and :276 (_setsid) take windowless_spawn.background_python() for argv[0], bound at call time like _detached (:262). A new proof stubs systemd-run/Popen, captures argv from both paths under a PATH with no python3, and asserts argv[0] == sys.executable.

clauses.claim: _spawn's systemd-run argv runs sys.executable, not 'python3', under a PATH holding no python3
_setsid's Popen argv runs sys.executable under the same PATH
the tooth reds when either path's argv[0] is put back to 'python3'

decisions.text: D1: remote.py _spawn and _setsid bind background_python at call time (ticket 0156856b1fae's lazy import) and use it as argv[0].
D2: proof test_the_linux_bus_spawn_runs_the_callers_interpreter.py, one tooth per clause, subprocess stubbed, no bus started.
